sources.title: Fondazione Umberto Eco, "Le biblioteche"
sources.note: Ring-shaped flat, reinforced floors, full-height corridor shelving (literature, comics, press/media, art) leading to the big study with comb-and-island bookcases (philosophy, science, history, semiotics, books by/on Eco); Stanza degli antichi with balcony on the Castello.

sources.title: Fondazione scrollwall galleries (Studio Curti Parini): rectified frontal photographs of bookcases A-S and of the Stanza degli antichi
sources.note: Bay and shelf counts below were made by looking at these 650 px images; captions give the subject of each lettered bookcase.

sources.title: CriticaLetteraria, "Un pomeriggio nella casa-biblioteca di Umberto Eco" (Nov 2022, photos Curti Parini)
sources.note: Room sequence salotto -> vestibolo -> corridoio -> studio; corridor photo (shelves one side only), two wide views of the study (comb/island units, desk, door with over-door shelves), salotto vitrines, piano, Stanza degli antichi.

sources.title: Andrea Zanni, visit of 24 Apr 2010 (Wikimedia Italia)
sources.note: "La libreria nel lunghissimo corridoio e solo la narrativa"; big room: on the right a whole bookcase of his own works in translation, far right books about him, central part with the "sezione dei cretini" and boxes; rare-book room a small all-wood "stanzino" with a big lens on the table.

sources.title: Lila Azam Zanganeh, Paris Review 185 (2008), Art of Fiction 197
sources.note: "labyrinth of corridors lined with bookcases that reach all the way up to extraordinarily high ceilings - thirty thousand volumes"; study with his complete works in translation; living room with the castle in the windows, glass cases of seashells and rare comics, a lute, recorders.

sources.title: Eco & Carriere, This Is Not the End of the Book (2011)
sources.note: 50,000 books in his various homes, 1,200 rare titles; the Castello Sforzesco library "right across from our building"; the rare collection is the Bibliotheca semiologica curiosa lunatica magica et pneumatica.

sources.title: BreraPlus, "The Idea of the Library" documentary page
sources.note: Moved house over thirty years ago for the books, strengthened the floor, filled the corridors with bookshelves, set aside the Room of the Ancients with a balcony overlooking the Castello Sforzesco.

sources.title: Rivista Studio, 8 May 2022 (Studiolo at the Braidense)
sources.note: 73 boxes = 1,328 volumes; "la stanza tutta per se originale di Eco era di forma ellittica, mentre quella in Braidense e rettangolare".

sources.title: ANSA, 4 May 2022, Studiolo Umberto Eco
sources.note: Rare books were kept "in una stanza con vista sul castello Sforzesco"; over 1,300 titles arranged as he ordered them; flutes, sticks, comics, Peanuts figures, dog testicles in formalin on the shelves.

sources.title: Biblioteca Nazionale Braidense OPAC, shelfmark ECO.xx (eco-sources/braidense_eco_all.csv, 2,105 records)
sources.note: Shelfmark ECO.<section>.<running no.>: the running number records the order the volumes had in the author's home (Braidense, May 2022, p. 6). ECO.01 = the books on the shelves of his library (997 running numbers used, max 1107; hermetica/curiosa), ECO.02 = the books kept elsewhere in the studiolo, on the desk for example (165, max 169; 19th-c. French sets), ECO.03 = the most precious books (37, max 77: Dee 1564, Bruno 1582, Khunrath 1609, Locke 1690 alongside incunabula), ECO.04 = the library's own section of Eco's publications, created as a research tool (102): not a shelf of the flat.

sources.title: Nuovo & Coletto, "Gli incunaboli di Umberto Eco", AIB Studi 62 (2022)
sources.note: 36 incunabula listed; fund displayed "nello stesso ordine ideato dal professore".

sources.title: Unibo / Artribune / Il Resto del Carlino, opening of the Biblioteca Eco in Bologna (July 2026)
sources.note: 32,000+ volumes reinstalled on 600 linear metres in 10 thematic rooms; the Milan shelves were surveyed one by one before the move; the density there (about 53 vols/m) is an upper bound for Milan.

rooms.name: Living room
rooms.blurb: Modern furnishings, the Castello Sforzesco in the windows, glass display cases with open antique illustrated books, seashells and rare comics, a lute and recorders (parisreview-2008, zanni-photo-2010). In 2022 the guided visit started here: art books, "libri da esposizione", encyclopaedias and atlases, and the vitrine in which Eco displayed the books of his current research (criticaletteraria-2022). The plaster statue and the three vitrines stand on the W wall beside the vestibule door, the cases 1.2 m out from the wall with the credenza and the dining table behind them, the curiosity cabinet and a second door on the E wall, the piano on the door wall; no wall of library books is in the room (bookcase E stands in the art corridor).

rooms.name: Entrance hall / vestibule
rooms.blurb: The 2022 visit passes from the salotto into a vestibule with a shelf for Joyce and shelves of Kabbalah, mystery, magic, the Templars, the devil and alchemy (criticaletteraria-2022), which matches Fondazione bookcases B and D. The turn-of-the-century lift lands the visitor in "a labyrinth of corridors lined with bookcases" (parisreview-2008). Drawn as a 3 x 4.5 m passage running from the salotto door to the corridor door (D on the corridor side, C on the end wall, B and the coats and prints opposite); the rare-book room opens off the start of the corridor just beyond it.

rooms.name: Room of the Ancients (rare-book room)
rooms.blurb: A small all-wood room with a balcony on the Castello Sforzesco, no telephone or computer, flutes and scores, the books shelved next to mirabilia - dog testicles in formalin, shells, coral, wooden models (ansa-2022, breraplus-idea, zanni-2010); the family recalls its original shape as elliptical, whereas the Braidense Studiolo that reproduces it is rectangular (rivista-studio-2022). It held the Bibliotheca semiologica curiosa lunatica magica et pneumatica, 1,328 volumes at the transfer of August 2021 (carriere-2011, braidense-opac, aib-2022). Braidense's catalogue documents the transferred collection and its ordering: the running number of a shelfmark records the order the volumes had in the author's home, ECO.01 the books on the shelves of the room, ECO.02 the books kept elsewhere in it (on the desk, for example), ECO.03 the most precious books. Its additional ECO.04 section brings together publications by Eco for research and does not by itself establish a copy's original position in the Milan apartment (braidense-studiolo-2022, p. 6).

rooms.catalog_note: Braidense ECO.xx shelfmarks (2,105 records in the export; the library counted 1,328 volumes at the transfer, and a record is not a volume: set records stand behind their volumes, works bound together share a shelfmark): ECO.01 the books on the shelves of the room (c. 1,570 records / 997 running numbers used up to 1107: hermetica, Kircher, Fludd, Rosicrucians, curiosa; median year 1719); ECO.02 the books kept elsewhere in the room, on the desk for example (372 records / 165 numbers to 169: 19th-c. French sets, Dumas, Sue, Peladan, "fous litteraires"; median 1856); ECO.03 the most precious books (51 records / 37 numbers to 77: Dee 1564, Bruno 1582, Khunrath 1609, Locke 1690 alongside incunabula; median 1563; 17 of Eco's 36 incunabula are absent from the Braidense export and are listed from AIB Studi 2022); ECO.04 the library's own reference section of Eco's publications (110 records / 102 numbers; Italian editions 1975-2025, most of them inventoried by the Braidense between 1996 and 2016, the rest from 2022 on): not a shelf of the flat, so its records are listed as reference entries and drawn on no cabinet. At 30-40 volumes per metre the three shelved runs need about 25-33 m + 6-8 m + 1-2.5 m = c. 32-44 shelf metres; the two wall units drawn below offer c. 80 m, consistent with loosely shelved folios and the mirabilia between them.

notes: Geometry is a reconstruction from photographs and visitor accounts; no floor plan of the apartment has been published. Room sizes, door positions and the assignment of bookcases to walls are estimates unless the evidence field says a photo or text supports them.

The Fondazione lettering A-S (Italian alphabet: no J, K) reads as a walk order: A corridor, B-D vestibule, E-H art, I-L philosophy wall, M-O islands, P semiotics wall, Q Eco's works, R-S psychology/sociology. Every bookcase id keeps its letter (study-P, corridor-07, rare-02).

Shelf counts are what the 650 px rectified photographs show: full-height units have 11 shelves (4 above a sliding-ladder rail at c. 2.3 m, 7 below), P has 10, low units 4-6. Two units (F, G) are cropped at the top and may have an 11th shelf.

Capacity check: 804 shelf metres of working-library shelving at 33-40 volumes per metre gives 26,545-32,176 volumes against the c. 33,000 counted by the Fondazione (32,000+ moved to Bologna). Bologna re-shelved them on 600 linear metres (53/m), so the Milan run was not full everywhere - the photos show gaps, piles lying flat and boxes on the floor.

Not modelled: piles on the piano, coffee table and desk; the "scatoloni ovunque" (2010); the Monte Cerignone house (c. 11,000 volumes); any bedroom or kitchen shelving - no source places bookcases there.

The Ferrario 2015 tracking walks and the 2022 film show the corridor and the study in motion; the bookcases are identified from the photographs, and the spines read from the frames of the 2022 film cite the second at which they appear.

For the builder: bookcases[].kind extends the schema with "island" (double-sided low unit; island_of/face group the faces), "cabinet" (glazed wood), "display" (glass vitrine) and "low"; door_span_m gives the doorway inside a door-surround unit (D, I); est_volumes and shelf_metres_m are derived fields.

ECO.03 is the "most precious books" section, not an incunabula section; it is drawn as its own glazed cabinet (rare-04) on the balcony wall, a guess; 17 of the 36 incunabula (AIB Studi 2022) are absent from the Braidense export and are added from the experience/incunabula list. The Stanza degli antichi opens off the START of the long corridor (print-wall side, near the vestibule), not at the end of the walk; rooms are ordered salotto, vestibolo, antichi, corridoio, corridoio-arte, studio, and the corridor carries a second door (doors_extra) for it.

The vestibule is drawn transposed (3 x 4.5 m) so that the salotto door (N), bookcase D with the corridor doorway (E) and the end wall with C (S) form the passage the 2015 take walks through; the corridor doorway is the D door bridge (1.45 m).

The salotto is drawn at 7.5 x 7.6 m from the wall sequences of the footage (eco-video/salotto/salotto_layout.json); bookcase E stands in the art corridor; the windows listed per room are drawn by the page.

ECO.04: the Braidense's account of its catalogue (press kit of 4 May 2022, p. 6) describes ECO.04 as a section created to gather the author's publications as research tools, unlike ECO.01 to ECO.03, which record the order the volumes had in the flat. The map therefore lists the ECO.04 records as reference entries on a table in the study and draws none of them on the low shelf at the door end (rare-03), whose contents are not identified.
